🎥🎬: Happiness (1998)

Behind the seemingly ordinary lives of several suburban New Jersey residents lies a disturbing web of loneliness, obsession, sexual frustration, and deeply buried secrets. The film follows three sisters and the people orbiting their lives, revealing the unsettling gap between how people present themselves and what they hide behind closed doors.

As their stories intertwine, each character searches for connection and satisfaction in increasingly troubling ways. Their desires expose the darker corners of human behaviour, challenging the idea that happiness is always something pure, simple, or easy to understand.

Uncomfortable, provocative, and deliberately unsettling, Happiness examines the loneliness and dysfunction beneath everyday life, forcing viewers to confront the disturbing realities people often refuse to acknowledge.

source_details.synopsis: Happiness is a 1998 American black comedy-drama film written and directed by Todd Solondz. It stars an ensemble cast consisting of Jane Adams, Elizabeth Ashley, Dylan Baker, Lara Flynn Boyle, Ben Gazzara, Jared Harris, Philip Seymour Hoffman, Louise Lasser, Jon Lovitz, Camryn Manheim, Rufus Read, and Cynthia Stevenson. The film revolves around the lives of three sisters (Adams, Boyle, and Stevenson), their parents (Gazzara and Lasser), their lovers (Baker, Harris, and Lovitz), and others around them (Ashley, Hoffman, Manheim, and Read).
